item.title: Pope Leo XIV faces crisis as a traditionalist group plans bishop consecrations without consent
item.description: VATICAN CITY (AP) — The Swiss-based Society of St. Pius X, which has schools, chapels and seminaries around the world, has been a thorn in the side of the Holy See for four decades, founded in opposition to the modernizing reforms of the 1960s Second Vatican Council. The post Pope Leo XIV faces crisis as a traditionalist group plans bishop consecrations without consent appeared first on RNS.

item.title: How women are reinterpreting the menstrual taboos in Chinese Buddhism
item.description: (The Conversation) — In some cultures, menstruation and childbirth are treated as polluting, not life-giving. One Buddhist text’s interpretation of ‘Blood Pond Hell’ shows how far such beliefs go – and how women respond. The post How women are reinterpreting the menstrual taboos in Chinese Buddhism appeared first on RNS.

item.title: At his installation, New York Archbishop Hicks commits to missionary church
item.description: NEW YORK (RNS) — At his installation Mass in St. Patrick’s Cathedral, Hicks made two things crystal clear: that he seeks to lead a church that will, at its heart, be missionary, and that Latinos will not remain at the peripheries of his ministry.
